title: Multiclass Logistic Regression and 2D Decision Regions on Iris
description: Select the first two Iris features iris.data[:, :2], fit a StandardScaler + LogisticRegression pipeline, report test accuracy, and plot the 3-class decision regions over a meshgrid.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Load `iris = load_iris()`, slice the first two feature columns `X = iris.data[:, :2]` and 3-class labels `y = iris.target`. Split using the supplied ratio with `stratify=y`.
Fit a `StandardScaler` and `LogisticRegression` pipeline on `(X_train, y_train)` using the supplied iteration limit. Print `clf.score(X_test, y_test)` (`0.763`).

Build a meshgrid `(xx, yy)` over the two features using the supplied resolution. Predict class labels `Z = clf.predict(grid).reshape(xx.shape)`. Fill the 3 decision regions with `plt.contourf` and overlay the data points `plt.scatter(X[:,0], X[:,1], c=y)`.

Look at lines 3 and 17-20: keeping only 2 features (`X = iris.data[:, :2]`) allows 2-column points for prediction. `grid = np.c_[xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()]` passes them directly into `clf.predict(grid)`. The supplied contour levels bracket the integer class labels `0, 1, 2`.

steps.question: Why does line 20 set the supplied contour levels when calling `plt.contourf(xx, yy, Z, ...)`?
steps.answer: The levels place contour boundaries halfway between the discrete class indices `0`, `1`, and `2` in `Z`.
